items.prompt: An instructor sends POST /learner/enrollments/<a learner's enrollment id>/complete with their own valid token. What happens?
items.answer: It succeeds, and the learner's enrollment is marked COMPLETED
distractors: 403, as only the enrolled learner may complete an enrollment
404, because the enrollment is looked up by the caller's user id
400, because the x-organization-id header was not sent with it
items.explanation: The learner router uses only requireAuth, and the complete route loads the enrollment by id alone; nothing compares enrollment.userId with the caller. Exercise 2 of the design doc proves and then fixes this.

items.prompt: A learner has completed 0 of 4 lessons and calls the complete route for their enrollment. What happens to it?
items.answer: It is set to COMPLETED, without a certificate
distractors: 409, and the status stays ACTIVE until every lesson is done
It is set to COMPLETED, and a certificate is issued too
400, because the course completion rule is not yet met
items.explanation: The route writes status COMPLETED before deciding anything, and canIssueCertificate then fails on completionPercent 0. The version's completion rule is never read.

items.prompt: An enrollment has all lessons completed, one passed quiz attempt, and no assignment submissions at all. What does the complete route do?
items.answer: It issues a certificate, as every() over no submissions is true
distractors: It withholds the certificate until an assignment has been graded
It refuses with 409 and asks for the assignment to be submitted
It marks it COMPLETED and leaves the certificate pending grading
items.explanation: requiredAssignmentsComplete is submissions.every(GRADED), and every() on an empty array returns true, so assignments are never actually required; all four canIssueCertificate inputs pass.

items.prompt: A learner who already received a certificate calls the complete route for the same enrollment a second time. What does the API return?
items.answer: 500 with the raw database error, because the certificate exists
distractors: 200 with the existing certificate, since the route is idempotent
409, because the route checks for an existing certificate first
200 with a second certificate under a new verification code
items.explanation: The update to COMPLETED runs again, then certificate.create hits the unique enrollmentId on Certificate. errorHandler maps only HttpError, so the Prisma error comes back as 500 with its message.

items.prompt: A course's version 1 is published. An instructor then starts version 2, which is still a draft. A new learner enrolls. Which version do they get?
items.answer: Version 2, the draft, as the highest version number wins
distractors: Version 1, which is the course's current published version
None: enrollment is refused while a draft exists
Version 1, until version 2 is published by someone
items.explanation: The enroll route takes versions ordered by versionNumber desc, take 1, with no status filter and without using Course.currentVersionId, so the draft wins.

items.prompt: A 2-point quiz question has correct options A and C. The learner selects only A. How many points does scoreQuiz award for that question?
items.answer: Zero, since the selection has to equal the correct set exactly
distractors: 1 point, which is half credit for one of the two right options
2 points, because A is one of the question's correct options
1 point, as a missing option costs half the question's value
items.explanation: scoreQuiz sorts both arrays and awards the full points only when they are equal; there is no partial credit, so [A] against [A, C] earns 0.

items.prompt: randomizeQuestionOrder is on for a quiz. Why does a learner's second attempt usually get a different question order than their first?
items.answer: The seed joins the enrollment id and the attempt number
distractors: The seed is the current time, so every request reshuffles
The seed is the quiz id, and answers are shuffled per call
It calls Math.random, so no two attempts ever line up
items.explanation: The route seeds selectRandomizedQuestionIds with `${enrollmentId}-${attemptCount + 1}`. The shuffle is deterministic for that seed, and the next attempt number changes it. The chosen order is stored as questionOrder.

items.prompt: A learner POSTs lesson progress with status "DONE", which is not one of the allowed values. Which HTTP status comes back?
items.answer: 500, with the raw validation message in the body
distractors: 400, with each of the zod issues listed in the response
422, as the body is well formed but invalid
404, as no progress row has the status DONE
items.explanation: z.enum(["IN_PROGRESS", "COMPLETED"]).parse throws a ZodError, which is not an HttpError, so errorHandler answers 500 with error.message.

items.prompt: A learner with two enrollments calls GET /learner/dashboard with a valid token but no x-organization-id header. What do they get?
distractors: 400 asking for the header first
200 with all of their enrollments
403 for a missing organization
items.explanation: The learner router has no organization middleware. The route turns the missing header into "" and filters enrollments on organizationId: "", which matches nothing.

items.prompt: A course has one published version whose completionRuleJson sets minimumQuizScore to 90. An instructor calls POST /authoring/courses/:courseId/versions. What is created?
items.answer: Version 2 as a DRAFT, with the minimum quiz score of 90 copied over
distractors: Version 2 as PUBLISHED, so new learners enroll in it at once
Version 2 as a DRAFT, with the rule reset to the default score of 80
Version 1 again, replacing the published row in place
items.explanation: The route loads the highest-numbered version, creates versionNumber latest + 1 with status DRAFT, and copies latest.completionRuleJson; the 80-point rule is only the fallback when no version exists. Publishing is a separate route.

items.prompt: An org admin bulk-imports a learner whose email already belongs to a user in another organization. What happens to that user?
items.answer: Their name changes, they are not added to the org, yet they count as imported
distractors: They get a LEARNER membership in the importing org and keep their name
The import fails with 409 because that email address is already taken
They are skipped, and the response lists them under a separate "existing" key
items.explanation: The import upserts by email: create adds the membership and the shared password, but update only sets name. The user is still pushed onto imported and counted in the audit.

items.prompt: During POST /learner/courses/:courseId/enroll, the lessonProgress.createMany call throws after the enrollment row was created. What is left in the database?
items.answer: The enrollment row, with no progress rows and no domain event
distractors: Nothing, since the enroll writes share a single transaction
The enrollment and its domain event, but no progress rows
The enrollment, whose progress rows the worker retries later
items.explanation: enrollment.create, lessonProgress.createMany and recordDomainEvent are separate awaited calls with no prisma.$transaction, so the enrollment stays committed and the event, written after createMany, is never recorded. No worker creates progress rows.

items.front: What does requireOrganizationRole prove, and what does it leave to each route?
items.back: It proves the caller holds one of the listed roles in the organization named by the x-organization-id header (400 if the header is missing, 403 if not). It does not prove that the course, version or submission being touched belongs to that organization; each route must check that itself, and most here do not.

items.front: List what POST /learner/enrollments/:id/complete does, in order.
items.back: Load the enrollment by id (404 if missing); compute lesson completion percent, whether any quiz attempt passed, and whether every submission is GRADED; set the enrollment to COMPLETED unconditionally; create a certificate only if canIssueCertificate passes; write an audit log; return both.

items.front: How does this API report a validation or database error?
items.back: errorHandler keeps the status only for HttpError. Any other Error, such as a ZodError or a Prisma unique violation, is returned as 500 with its raw message; non-Error values get 500 "Unexpected server error".

items.front: Why do learners enroll in a CourseVersion rather than in a Course?
items.back: So later authoring changes do not rewrite what a learner completed: the enrollment, its lesson progress and its certificate point at the exact version taken. That only works if enrollment picks a published version, which this snapshot does not guarantee.
